app.title: The Moon Remembers
app.subtitle: A Lunar Journey with Cuội and the Forgotten Rover
app.hook: When a mission ends, the story does not. A small rover, a woodcutter from a very old story, and a message that took fifty years to arrive.

sources.heading: Sources and honesty
sources.sub: Every fact in this game comes from a public source. Here's how to check it.
sources.realBody: Photos, the Moon and Mars maps, dates, distances, mission facts, and hardware status are taken from NASA, JPL, and USGS.
sources.simplifiedBody: Echo and Archive Control are fictional. Most 3D spacecraft are NASA's own published models; Ranger, Surveyor, the laser mirror, the Lunar Rover, and Sojourner are hand-built approximations. Landing, driving, orbit, and battery simulations use real physics ideas with shortened distances and times. Landing-site puzzles and soil charts are illustrations, not data.
sources.date: Facts were checked in November 2026. Missions change, so visit NASA for the latest.
sources.flipbookNotice: The storybook uses the GUL Labs flipbook React binding and its MPL-licensed core. License text and package attribution:

laserlab.about: Astronauts left mirrors on the Moon. Bounce a laser off one, and the time it takes to come back tells you how far away the Moon is.

interlude.title: The first time I climbed the tree
interlude.line1: When I was young, I tried to climb the banyan tree every morning. For a long time, I fell at the same branch.
interlude.line2: I thought the tree was telling me to stop. Then my mother said: the tree is telling you where to put your hands.
interlude.line3: The third time I fell, I looked at the branch instead of the ground. The next morning, I climbed past it.
interlude.line4: You are not failing. You are learning where the branch is. Let us look again together.
interlude.hint: A hint is on now. The Moon is patient, and so are we.

archive.title: The instrument that listened
archive.intro: Cuội places the banyan leaf beside the silent package. The leaf glows, and the dust begins to remember.
archive.disclaimer: This memory archive is imagined. The leaf is a story symbol: it did not repair or restart anything.
archive.source: Facts checked against NASA and LPI sources.

cards.title: A small package
cards.body: Apollo 11 left the Early Apollo Scientific Experiments Package, EASEP, in 1969. Its seismic package, PSEP, was one part of it. A laser reflector was deployed at the same site, though it was not attached to EASEP.

cards.title: What it heard
cards.body: PSEP carried long-period and short-period seismometers. It listened for moonquakes, meteoroid impacts, and movements inside the Moon.

cards.title: Three weeks of listening
cards.body: It was switched on by ground command on 21 July 1969. It returned data for about three weeks of lunar daytime, then lost its command link in late August 1969. It was formally terminated on 27 August 1969, before its planned support phase was over.

cards.title: The data stayed
cards.body: The instrument is silent, but its record is still used. A machine can stop operating while what it measured keeps teaching.
